sections.h2: Who sends the bill and who answers questions
sections.html:
Almost every LaRue County tax office sits inside the courthouse complex on West High Street in Hodgenville, and Hodgenville homeowners get a second bill from City Hall. The sheriff sends and collects the county bill, the PVA sets the value, the clerk takes in bills left unpaid, and the county attorney works on delinquent ones.

  • Sheriff's Office. 209 West High Street, Suite 6; open weekdays from morning until four; (270) 358-3120.
  • Property valuation administrator. Value, exemptions and appeal conferences; (270) 358-4202.
  • County clerk. Suite 3 at the same address; open until 4:30 on weekdays; (270) 358-3544.
  • County attorney. Suite 8; (270) 358-9223.
  • Hodgenville City Hall. 200 S. Lincoln Blvd.; (270) 358-3832 for the city bill.

Call the PVA before paying when a figure looks off. The sheriff collects whatever amount the bill shows and has no say over value.

sections.h2: LaRue County housing at a glance
sections.html: LaRue is a rural county of gentle hills just outside the Bluegrass, with Hodgenville as the seat. It grew from 14,867 residents in 2020 to an estimated 15,184 in July 2025 and holds 6,763 housing units. The median home value among owner-occupants is $183,500, and 79.4 percent of the 5,996 households own. Median rent is $860. Higher values mean larger tax bills at the same rate, which makes a clean payoff worth the effort before listing. LaRue is also a dry county, which matters to anyone selling a building for restaurant use.

The county attorney's office says bills typically mail in October, carry a December 31 due date, and can be paid at the sheriff's desk from November 1 through April 15. The 2026 bills went out on October 30, 2026, and the city bills were mailed around the same time.

Payment steps for 2026 LaRue County bills
Paid betweenAmount owed
Nov. 1 to Nov. 30, 20262% discount off the bill
Dec. 1 to Dec. 31, 2026Exactly the bill amount
Jan. 1 to Jan. 31, 2027Bill amount with 5% added
Feb. 1, 2027 onwardBill amount with 10% added, plus a possible 11% sheriff's fee on county bills

A card payment online adds a 2.5 percent fee. Inside the courthouse foyer, a drop box takes payments at any hour. By mail, enclose the bill or its number, plus a stamped return envelope if you want a receipt. These steps are reset each year, so check the bill itself.

sections.h2: Is there a separate Hodgenville city tax bill?
sections.html:
Yes. A parcel inside the city gets a county bill from the sheriff and a city bill from City Hall, and the two are paid in different places. City payments go to City Hall, the city website or the city drop box, and the same November 30 cutoff earns the 2 percent discount. A parcel outside the city limits gets only the county bill.

When you buy or sell in Hodgenville, ask the closing agent to confirm that both bills are paid or prorated. The sheriff's office also has a fire dues waiver form. The online portal cannot remove fire dues, so an owner seeking a waiver files it at the sheriff's office.

Ask the PVA, at (270) 358-4202, for a conference. Kentucky requires one before any appeal. The valuation date is January 1, and the tax roll opens for inspection in early May. After that conference the appeal goes to the county clerk right after the inspection period ends, and a board of local property owners hears it within weeks.

The board denies a case that arrives without evidence, so assemble recent sales of similar homes, an appraisal, repair bids or insurance values. The county attorney's office helps the PVA with assessment appeals.

sections.h2: What happens to an unpaid bill
sections.html:
A bill still open on April 15 passes to the clerk as a certificate of delinquency, which is a lien on the real estate under KRS 134.122. Whoever owned the property on January 1 of that tax year also owes the bill personally. Penalties and fees are added, and interest at 12 percent a year under KRS 134.125 makes the total rise every month.

  • The county attorney mails two notices before any certificate is sold.
  • After 90 days, KRS 134.452 lets outside buyers purchase it by paying the amount due.
  • The first batch of certificates is usually offered at a tax bill sale in August.
  • An unsold certificate is paid at the clerk's office, Suite 3, 209 W. High Street.
  • A certificate that has been sold must be paid to the buyer.

A certificate cannot be sold while a payment agreement with the county attorney is in place or while the parcel is tied up in foreclosure or bankruptcy litigation that includes that office. The county attorney arranges payment plans on unsold certificates at (270) 358-9223.

The state set the deduction at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. It is available to owners who have reached 65 or who are totally disabled under a retirement system, for a home they own and occupy on January 1. Apply to the PVA, (270) 358-4202, by the end of December.

The deduction lowers assessed value, so the savings depend on the combined county, school, city and district rates on your parcel. Heirs who take over a house should ask the PVA what changes once the title moves.

sections.h2: Who pays what when a house changes hands
sections.html:
The January 1 owner is the person on that year's bill, so a spring closing still leaves the seller named. The settlement statement usually divides the year, and the closing agent pays the sheriff. The deed must carry an in-care-of address for the transfer-year bill under KRS 382.135(1)(d), which means giving the buyer's mailing address.

Before listing a LaRue County house with back taxes, collect two numbers: the current-year amount from the sheriff and any delinquent certificate balance from the clerk. Houses that were inherited, behind on payments or too worn for a standard listing can often close faster in a direct cash sale, and the payoffs come out of that one closing as long as they were requested ahead of time.

sections.h2: Paying at the courthouse: a short checklist
sections.html:
Walk-in payments go to Suite 6 at 209 West High Street. Bring the bill, or at least the bill number, so the clerk behind the desk can pull the right parcel. If you live in Hodgenville, plan on two stops or two payments, since City Hall takes the city bill at 200 S. Lincoln Blvd. Keep both receipts with your closing file.

If you are selling, call the sheriff and the clerk before you set a closing date. Ask for the current-year amount, ask whether any certificate is open, and ask how long each figure stays good. A written payoff from each office lets the title company work from real numbers instead of estimates, and it keeps a late discovery from pushing your sale back.

faqs.q: Who takes LaRue County property tax payments?
faqs.a: The sheriff's office at 209 West High Street, Suite 6, by mail, online or in the courthouse drop box. Hodgenville city bills go to City Hall at 200 S. Lincoln Blvd.

faqs.q: When does the 2026 LaRue County discount end?
faqs.a: Payments made through November 30, 2026 earn a 2% discount. December 1 through 31 requires the face amount, January 2027 adds 5%, and after that the penalty is 10%.

faqs.q: How fast does a late LaRue County bill grow?
faqs.a: After April 15 it becomes a certificate of delinquency that earns 12 percent interest a year, plus penalties and fees. The county attorney can discuss a plan if the certificate is unsold.

faqs.q: Where do I sign up for the LaRue County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: At the PVA, (270) 358-4202, before December 31. Qualifying owners are 65 or older, or totally disabled under a retirement system, and must own and occupy the home on January 1.

faqs.q: May I sell a LaRue County house while taxes are overdue?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien stays on the parcel, so the payoff is deducted at closing. Get written amounts from the sheriff and the clerk before picking a date.
